text:
ash: thinking about an "attenuated degrade" fallback mode — instead of full-mode failover we'd return a short partial result (first 50 tokens or a cached summary) when we hit transient errors. keeps latency low for callers. open to feedback :thinking_face:
neel: curious about triggers. do we mean any 5xx or only specific model-exec errors? also need to avoid double-chaining with client retries
taylor: +1 for partial responses, but we need clear auditability. any auto-fallback must record a snapshot of inputs, model-version, route, and policy that kicked in
ben: also quota implications — if we return partial then downstream billing and usage attribution changes. we should surface a separate counter in console: autodegrade.count and autodegrade.sampled_requests
sasha: can we make sampling configurable? e.g. keep 100% breadcrumbs for the first minute of a rollout then downsample to 1%
nash: @sasha +1. UX for configuring that in the rollout UI needs quick toggles: sample rate slider + retention dropdown (30d/90d/365d)
neel: on triggers: propose a compound rule: (p95_latency > 750ms for 2m) OR (error_rate_5xx > 3% for 1m) OR (kv_cache_miss_rate spike > 20% for 3m)
ben: love that. add a cooldown window to avoid oscillation (e.g. 5m lock after a fallback)
taylor: audit requirements — we must store enough to replay decisions. minimally: request_id, route, model_version, policy_id, signal_values, timestamp, outcome
ash: what about privacy? some customers send PII. we should mark autodegrade snapshots as redacted by default and provide a way for customers to opt-in to full payload retention
sasha: UX idea: in the rollout console show a "Degrade Preview" that simulates how responses would look (sampled from logs or synthetic inputs) along with expected cost delta
ash: policy-bot: proposed config prototype:
```
{
  "policy_id": "auto-fallback-v2",
  "mode": "attenuated-degrade",
  "triggers": [
    {"signal": "p95_latency_ms", "op": ">", "value": 750, "window": "2m"},
    {"signal": "error_rate_5xx", "op": ">", "value": 0.03, "window": "1m"}
  ],
  "sample_policy": {"initial_rate": 1.0, "decay_to": 0.01, "decay_after": "10m"},
  "cooldown": "5m",
  "audit": {"retention_days": 30, "redact_payload": true}
}
```
neel: config looks good. one suggestion: add a "safety_score" threshold so we can tie into A/B rollback heuristics (if user-defined metric drops > X then immediate full rollback)
ben: agree, also need to emit telemetry events for each state transition: policy.evaluated, policy.triggered, policy.entered, policy.exited. those should be queryable in Logs and appear on the model route timeline
taylor: on API surface: should we expose a new header so callers can detect degraded responses e.g. `X-Redwood-Degraded: attenuated-v2` and maybe `X-Redwood-Degrade-Sample: true`
ash: yes exposing headers/small metadata is important. also we should define canonical partial response schema so SDKs can handle it gracefully
sasha: for the console, tiny microcopy is key — show "Why did my request degrade?" with links to the audit snapshot and a one-line reason like "p95 latency exceeded 750ms"
neel: implementation note: runtime needs to be able to return cached summaries cheaply. we may need a background job to precompute summarizations for hot prefixes
ash: ops question — how do we test this in dedicated vs hosted customers? need a canary rollout that only affects 5% of traffic and allows sim-mode (evaluate triggers but don't actually change responses)
policy-bot: deploy note: auto-fallback-v2 config pushed to staging at 2775014000, simulated traffic run started :rocket:
ben: after staging verification, schedule gradual ramp: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback if safety_score drops 2 std devs
taylor: docs needed: API header spec, partial-response schema, telemetry event reference, and console flows (preview + audit explorer)
sasha: i'll draft the console mocks, will include sampling controls and a timeline chart showing sampled snapshots
ash: thanks team. next steps: neel to finalize trigger definitions, ben to wire telemetry events, taylor to spec headers/SDKs, sasha to mock UI. follow-up sync tomorrow 10am PT
neel: noted. will add acceptance tests for oscillation protection
ben: will make an alert runbook for SRE and include playbook steps for disabling autodegrade via API
taylor: SDK change list + changelog entry on my plate
sasha: mock links coming in a thread reply later :white_check_mark:
policy-bot: policy push to staging succeeded at 2775014967, no critical errors detected
ash: awesome. thanks everyone :clap:
